title: Matignon's Cipher-1, 1584: letter of BnF fr. 15568 ff. 151r-152r (catalogue 2840, read in part) and fr. 15567 f. 24 (catalogue 2838, decoded, not read), with Tomokiyo's table

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 15568 ff. 151r-152r (Gallica btv1b9063927n; view = folio + 8: f. 151r = view 159 right, f. 151v = view 160 left, f. 152r = view 160 right, endorsement f. 153 = view 161). Images: Source gallica.bnf.fr / BnF
documents.route: Jacques de Matignon (docket f. 153 'M. le mareschal de Matignon ... 1584') -> unknown

plaintext.source: A few words glossed in letters between the lines of f. 151r by a period hand: l. 1 'f∴soi' over the decode 'fesoi', l. 3 '...o[m]iacen', a gloss beginning with the que sign, and 'a ue' (or 'a ne') over 4 □. No decipherment on the neighbouring leaves (views 157-164). Tomokiyo names f. 151 under Matignon's Cipher-1 and gives no reading.

transcription.source: Brice Dudout with Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), from deskewed line crops of the Gallica full-size images (Source gallica.bnf.fr / BnF). Every line in two independent passes (one blind sub-agent per pass); the two held-out portions arbitrated on the image without a key, the development lines arbitrated by sense.
transcription.notes: Folio numbers follow Daniel Bourdeau's correction: Gallica view = folio + 8. Agreement of the two passes before arbitration: 88.6% (f. 151v), 88.8% (f. 151r). Hard shapes: 6/6^, st/long s, rho/looped f, e/z-like 3.

plaintext.source: A contemporary decipherment in letters, written between the lines over almost every cipher line of f. 85r (the BnF catalogue describes the piece as 'en chiffre, avec déchiffrement'). It is the existing reading of this leaf; this project has not transcribed it and claims no reading. The leaf was used only to test the key (test E2).

transcription.notes: Another hand, with sign forms absent from the key (new labels decode as '?').

system.summary: Matignon's Cipher-1 (Tomokiyo's table): homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with code signs (barred theta = le roy, diamond with tail = que) and nulls.
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's Matignon's Cipher-1 table (cryptiana henryiii.htm), reconstructed from fr. 15567 ff. 24, 54
system.notes: Different system from the Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1 (matignon1586) and from Matignon's Cipher-3 (matignon1586c3) and tuple cipher (matignon1586tuple).

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo publishes the table and says f. 151 uses it, without a reading; no issue, PR or lead on fr. 15568 in this repository (checked 16 Nov 2026)

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout directed the work; Claude Opus 5.5 transcribed, extended the key and ran the pre-registered test.

solution.what: Test A. Tomokiyo's table extended on f. 151r, frozen as holdout/key_frozen.tsv (sha256 913f766d...461b), and measured once on a held-out portion (f. 152r + last line of f. 151v, 302 signs) chosen before transcription: 262/299 signs (87.6%) in sense runs; 200 shuffled keys max 32.1%; pre-set bar 0.85 and max+0.30 met.

Test C, a re-test after development changes: the key was corrected on the development lines of ff. 151r-v and frozen as retest_C/key_C.tsv (sha256 ff5f1221...5b90, PREREG-C2), then measured once on a new held-out portion (f. 151v ll. 1-9, 377 signs) chosen and frozen before transcription (PREREG-C): 287/374 signs (76.7%) in sense runs; 200 shuffled keys max 34.5%. The pre-set bar 0.85 is NOT met (the second bar, max + 0.30, is). A clerical slip left sign 6 without a value in key_C.tsv; a post-hoc, non-probative rerun with 6 = p gives 73.0%.

Test D, a re-test after a further development change: key_D.tsv = key.tsv (sha256 eb00fd85...3404) = key_C.tsv + 6 = p, frozen in PREREG-D before f. 24 was transcribed. Single measure on a new document (fr. 15567 f. 24, catalogue 2838, ll. 2-10, 387 labels, chosen and frozen before transcription, transcription frozen before decoding in PREREG-D2): 294/385 signs (76.4%) in sense runs; 200 shuffled keys median 2.6%, max 27.8%. The pre-set bar 0.85 is NOT met (max + 0.30 is). f24/test_D/.

Test E1, a re-test of the same key after the development changes above: key_D.tsv (sha256 eb00fd85...3404, unchanged since test D). Portion fr. 15567 f. 54r cipher ll. 3-12 chosen and frozen before transcription (siblings/PREREG-E.md, sha256 f5542ba2...93df); two blind passes, arbitrated on the image without a key, frozen with the scripts before decoding (siblings/PREREG-E2.md, sha256 dcc633d7...b8de); one run of siblings/scripts/run_measure_E.sh: 321/432 signs (74.3%) in sense runs; 200 shuffled keys median 2.1%, max 34.7%. The bar 0.85 is NOT met. Not fully independent: Tomokiyo built his table partly from f. 54. After the test, strict read share 44/83 = 0.530 (siblings/lecture/E1_reading_marked.txt): decoded, not read.

Test E2, a re-test of the same key after the development changes above: key_D.tsv (sha256 eb00fd85...3404, unchanged). Portion fr. 3255 f. 85r cipher ll. 1-16 (456 signs), under the same PREREG-E / PREREG-E2 freeze and the same single run as E1: 205/456 signs (45.0%) in sense runs; 200 shuffled keys median 0.0%, max 42.5%. Both bars fail. The leaf carries a period interlinear decipherment (existing), not used in the test; its hand has sign forms the key does not cover.

Integration review of PR #709: strict share of ff. 151r-152r recounted by whole words (a space-separated word with any {}, [], angle bracket or ? counts as a hole) on texts/reading_marked.txt: sure 373, probable 84, restored 2, unresolved 230 of 689 words, strict 373/689 = 0.541 (filed 377/693 = 0.544: scripts/count_marked.py splits a word with a restored letter, e.g. compa[g]nies, and counts the outer pieces as sure words). The same rule gives E1 44/83 and f. 24 38/93, as filed. Class unchanged.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's Matignon's Cipher-1 table extended on development lines of ff. 151r-v; five single pre-registered tests: A passed (0.876, holdout/key_frozen.tsv); C (0.767, retest_C/key_C.tsv), D (0.764, fr. 15567 f. 24), E1 (0.743, fr. 15567 f. 54) and E2 (0.450, fr. 3255 f. 85), the last three with key_D.tsv = key.tsv, are below the 0.85 bar.

texts.summary: Report from Marshal Matignon's side (1584, docket f. 153) on Huguenot moves in Guyenne: the king of Navarre's men gaining a foothold in the province and refusing to give back the towns of surety, the writer's loyalty to the king alone, La Rochefoucauld's arrival beside the king of Navarre, and the king of Navarre's claim that Henri III allowed him to build at Le Boucau, at the mouth of the Adour below Bayonne.

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #709 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Read as sentences against texts/decryption.txt: the legible passages (service to the king alone, the Huguenots and the towns of surety, La Rochefoucauld beside the king of Navarre, Le Boucau) build sentences; long runs unresolved (230 words). Strict whole-word share 373/689 = 0.541, read in part. Key passed one of five pre-registered tests (A 0.876); C, D, E1, E2 failed the 0.85 bar.

texts.summary: Fragments: a rumour of which many people [speak], the King wants to do..., having a castle surprised, employing [men] in his provinces, 'prudence acoustumee', 'meschans bruictz contre l'honneur du roy'.
texts.note: Strict share 38/93 = 0.409 (sure + probable 0.570); held-out ll. 2-10 strict 0.480. Phrases hold, sentences do not.
